Several claims are overstated or wrong, and the next steps are generic and do not follow the narrative's own advice, so an investigator would have to redo some of the work.","problems":["Next steps are generic. They ask for a larger sample and a re-screen, but do not name the low-complexity 99215 claims (C0133517, C0133585, C0133765, C0133771) that the narrative says to request first.","The narrative says the 99214 claims on 0-condition visits (C0133752, C0133776, Z09) suggest the elevated coding 'may extend beyond 99215'. Two claims coded Z09 are weak evidence, and the 99214 documentation rate is 0% below billed. The inference is overreaching.","'Every one of the 16 returned charts supported the billed level' is not directly shown. The card gives 0 below billed, but this is not the same as confirming support. One 99215 chart has no recorded minutes.","'No sign of cloned documentation' goes beyond the evidence. The lab-line check does not test for cloning.","The headline says 'across every complexity band', but the 0-condition band has only 3 of 31 visits at 99215 (9.7%). The 'several times' claim is not quantified per band.","The narrative says C0133658 is a 5-condition patient, and that is true, but it does not note that the chart was documented as high MDM for a high-complexity patient. This is a minor gap.","The cited claims are only two low-complexity examples (C0133517 and C0133535). C0133535 has CKD and is not a clear simple-diagnosis case. The back pain claims are mentioned in the narrative but not cited.","It does not state that 0 documented 99215s were low-complexity, and a missing-data flag is limited to 'too thin'."]}
